questions.text: निर्देशकों द्वारा माँगे जाने से पूर्व अंशधारकों से प्राप्त अग्रिम धन राशि का लेखा :
questions.text_english: Money received in advance from the shareholders before it is actually called up by the directors is:

options.A: अग्रिम याचना खाते के जमा पक्ष में किया जाता है।
options.B: अग्रिम याचना खाते के नाम पक्ष में किया जाता है।
options.C: याचना खाते के जमा पक्ष में किया जाता है।
options.D: अदत्त याचना खाते के नाम पक्ष में किया जाता है।

options_english.A: credited to calls in advance account.
options_english.B: debited to calls in advance account.
options_english.D: debited to calls in arrears account.

questions.solution: The correct option is (A). Any amount paid by shareholders before the company explicitly makes a call represents a liability to the company until the call becomes due. Therefore, it is credited to a specific liability account known as the 'Calls in Advance Account'.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। जब कम्पनी अंशधारकों से वह राशि प्राप्त कर लेती है जिसकी याचना निर्देशकों द्वारा अभी तक नहीं की गई है, तो यह राशि कम्पनी के लिए एक देयता होती है। अतः इसे 'अग्रिम याचना खाते' में जमा (credit) किया जाता है।

sub_questions.text: मिशा, सरिता तथा ईशा एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2024 से उन्होंने निर्णय लिया कि वे लाभ-हानि को बराबर-बराबर बाँटेंगे। लाभ विभाजन अनुपात में परिवर्तन के कारण साझेदारों का अधिलाभ अथवा त्याग होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Misha, Sarita and Isha were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:1. With effect from 1st April 2024, they decided that they will share profits and losses equally. The gain or sacrifice by the partners due to change in profit sharing ratio will be:

options.A: मिशा का त्याग 1/6, ईशा का अधिलाभ 1/6
options.B: मिशा का अधिलाभ 1/6, ईशा का त्याग 1/6
options.C: मिशा का त्याग 1/6, सरिता का अधिलाभ 1/3, ईशा का त्याग 1/6
options.D: मिशा का त्याग 1/3, ईशा का अधिलाभ 1/3

options_english.C: Misha's sacrifice 1/6, Sarita's gain 1/3, Isha's sacrifice 1/6

sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (A). The old ratio is 3:2:1 (3/6, 2/6, 1/6). The new ratio is equal, i.e., 1:1:1 (2/6, 2/6, 2/6). We calculate the difference (Old Share - New Share): Misha: 3/6 - 2/6 = 1/6 (Sacrifice). Sarita: 2/6 - 2/6 = 0 (No change). Isha: 1/6 - 2/6 = -1/6 (Gain). Thus, Misha sacrifices 1/6 and Isha gains 1/6.

sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (B). Unless agreed otherwise, upon the death or retirement of a partner, the remaining partners are assumed to acquire the deceased partner's share in their existing relative profit-sharing ratio. The existing ratio between Sia and Aryan is 4:1.

questions.text: अनुज तथा कार्तिक एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:4 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2023 से आरम्भ कर 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में प्रत्येक वैकल्पिक महीने के आरम्भ में अनुज ने ₹ 20,000 का आहरण किया। 6% वार्षिक दर से 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में अनुज के आहरण पर ब्याज होगा :
questions.text_english: Anuj and Kartik were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:4. Anuj withdrew ₹ 20,000 in the beginning of every alternate month starting from 1st April, 2023 during the year ended 31st March, 2024. Interest on Anuj's drawings @ 6% p.a. for the year ended 31st March, 2024 will be:
questions.solution: The correct option is (C). Anuj withdraws ₹ 20,000 at the beginning of every alternate month, meaning he makes 6 withdrawals in a year. Total drawings = ₹ 20,000 × 6 = ₹ 1,20,000. The average period for drawings made at the beginning of alternate months is calculated as (Months left after first drawing + Months left after last drawing) / 2 = (12 + 2) / 2 = 7 months. The interest on drawings is: ₹ 1,20,000 × (6/100) × (7/12) = ₹ 4,200.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (C) है। अनुज प्रत्येक वैकल्पिक महीने के आरम्भ में ₹ 20,000 का आहरण करता है, इसलिए वर्ष में कुल 6 बार आहरण होंगे। कुल आहरण = ₹ 20,000 × 6 = ₹ 1,20,000. औसत अवधि = (प्रथम आहरण के बाद बचे माह + अंतिम आहरण के बाद बचे माह) / 2 = (12 + 2) / 2 = 7 माह। ब्याज की गणना = ₹ 1,20,000 × (6/100) × (7/12) = ₹ 4,200 होगी।

sub_questions.text: विशेष, माणिक तथा अमित एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:4:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 31 मार्च, 2024 को अमित सेवा निवृत्त हो गया। विशेष तथा माणिक ने अमित के भाग का अधिग्रहण 2:3 के अनुपात में किया। अमित की सेवा निवृत्ति के पश्चात विशेष तथा माणिक का नया लाभ विभाजन अनुपात होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Vishesh, Manik and Amit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:4:1. Amit retired on 31st March, 2024. Vishesh and Manik acquired Amit's share in the ratio of 2:3. The new profit sharing ratio between Vishesh and Manik after Amit's retirement will be:
sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (D). Amit's retiring share is 1/10. Vishesh acquires 2/5th of Amit's share, meaning 2/5 × 1/10 = 2/50. Manik acquires 3/5th of Amit's share, meaning 3/5 × 1/10 = 3/50. Vishesh's new share = Old share (5/10) + Gained share (2/50) = 25/50 + 2/50 = 27/50. Manik's new share = Old share (4/10) + Gained share (3/50) = 20/50 + 3/50 = 23/50. Therefore, the new ratio is 27:23.

sub_questions.text: वर्षा, आर्यन तथा निमित एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 2:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। वर्षा सेवा निवृत्त हो गयी तथा उसने अपने भाग का 1/3 भाग आर्यन के पक्ष में समर्पित किया तथा शेष भाग निमित के पक्ष में। आर्यन तथा निमित के मध्य नया लाभ विभाजन अनुपात होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Varsha, Aryan and Nimit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:2:1. Varsha retired and surrendered 1/3rd of her share in favour of Aryan and the remaining share in favour of Nimit. The new profit sharing ratio between Aryan and Nimit will be :
sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (B). Varsha's original share is 2/5. She surrenders 1/3rd of it to Aryan, so Aryan's gain = (1/3) × (2/5) = 2/15. The remaining 2/3rd goes to Nimit, so Nimit's gain = (2/3) × (2/5) = 4/15. Aryan's new share = Old share (2/5) + Gain (2/15) = (6/15 + 2/15) = 8/15. Nimit's new share = Old share (1/5) + Gain (4/15) = (3/15 + 4/15) = 7/15. The new ratio is 8:7.

questions.text: जब साझेदारों की पूँजी स्थायी होती है तो एक साझेदार द्वारा किये गये आहरणों का लेखा किया जाता है :
questions.text_english: When the partners' capitals are fixed, the drawings made by a partner are recorded on the :

options.A: साझेदार के पूँजी खाते के नाम पक्ष में
options.B: साझेदार के पूँजी खाते के जमा पक्ष में
options.C: साझेदार के चालू खाते के नाम पक्ष में
options.D: साझेदार के चालू खाते के जमा पक्ष में

options_english.A: Debit side of Partner's Capital Account.
options_english.B: Credit side of Partner's Capital Account.
options_english.C: Debit side of Partner's Current Account.
options_english.D: Credit side of Partner's Current Account.

questions.solution: The correct option is (C). Under the fixed capital system, the partners maintain both a Capital Account and a Current Account. All regular transactions like drawings out of profits, interest on capital, and salary are recorded in the Current Account. Drawings represent a withdrawal of funds and thus decrease the current account balance, meaning they are debited to the Current Account.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (C) है। स्थायी पूँजी पद्धति में साझेदार के दो खाते बनाए जाते हैं: पूँजी खाता और चालू खाता। लाभ में से किए गए आहरणों को साझेदार के चालू खाते के नाम (Debit) पक्ष में लिखा जाता है।

questions.text: ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 4,000 अंशों का हरण ₹ 2 प्रति अंश की दूसरी तथा अन्तिम याचना राशि का भुगतान न करने पर किया गया। इन अंशों के पुनः निर्गमन पर कम्पनी द्वारा आवश्यक रूप से एकत्रित की जाने वाली न्यूनतम राशि होगी :
questions.text_english: 4,000 shares of ₹ 10 each were forfeited for non-payment of second and final call money of ₹ 2 per share. The minimum amount that the company must collect at the time of reissue of these shares will be:
questions.solution: The correct option is (A). A company is permitted to reissue forfeited shares at a discount, but the maximum discount allowed is equal to the amount previously collected on those shares. On 4,000 shares, ₹ 8 per share was already paid (since only ₹ 2 was unpaid). The maximum discount is 4,000 × ₹ 8 = ₹ 32,000. Therefore, the minimum amount the company must collect on reissue is the total face value (₹ 40,000) minus the maximum allowable discount (₹ 32,000), which equates to ₹ 8,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। कम्पनी हरण किए गए अंशों को बट्टे पर पुनः निर्गमित कर सकती है, लेकिन यह बट्टा हरण किए गए अंशों पर पहले से प्राप्त राशि से अधिक नहीं हो सकता। 4,000 अंशों पर पहले ही ₹ 8 प्रति अंश (₹ 32,000) प्राप्त हो चुके थे। इसलिए कम्पनी को 4,000 अंशों पर न्यूनतम ₹ 8,000 (कुल ₹ 40,000 - ₹ 32,000) अवश्य एकत्रित करने होंगे।

questions.text: 1 अप्रैल, 2023 को वीबी लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 20,000, 13% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 10% बट्टे पर किया जिनका शोधन 4 वर्षों के पश्चात 5% प्रीमियम पर किया जाएगा। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त होने वाले वर्ष के लिए ऋणपत्रों पर ब्याज की कुल राशि होगी :
questions.text_english: On 1st April 2023, Veebee Ltd. issued 20,000, 13% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a discount of 10% redeemable at a premium of 5% after 4 years. Total amount of interest on debentures for the year ending 31st March, 2024 will be:
questions.solution: The correct option is (B). Interest on debentures is always calculated on the nominal or face value of the debentures issued, irrespective of any discount or premium on issue or redemption. The total face value of the debentures is 20,000 shares × ₹ 100 = ₹ 20,00,000. The interest for one year at 13% is calculated as ₹ 20,00,000 × 13% = ₹ 2,60,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (B) है। ऋणपत्रों पर ब्याज की गणना हमेशा उनके अंकित मूल्य (Face Value) पर की जाती है। कुल अंकित मूल्य = 20,000 × ₹ 100 = ₹ 20,00,000 है। 13% की दर से एक वर्ष का ब्याज = ₹ 20,00,000 × 13% = ₹ 2,60,000 होगा।

questions.text: आरुषि, विवान तथा मिताली एक फर्म के साझेदार थे। 31 मार्च, 2024 को फर्म का विघटन हो गया। उस तिथि को फर्म की पुस्तकों में ₹ 60,000 के देनदार तथा ₹ 3,000 संदिग्ध ऋणों के लिए प्रावधान विद्यमान था। ₹ 8,000 के देनदार डूब गये तथा शेष देनदारों से पूरी राशि वसूल हो गयी। देनदारों से वसूली गई राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Arushi, Vivaan and Mitali were partners in a firm. On 31st March 2024, the firm was dissolved. On that date the firm had debtors of ₹ 60,000 and provision for doubtful debts of ₹ 3,000 were existing in the books. Debtors of ₹ 8,000 proved bad and full amount was realised from the remaining debtors. The amount realised from debtors was:
questions.solution: The correct option is (C). At the time of dissolution, gross debtors of ₹ 60,000 are transferred to the debit side of the Realisation Account. When realizing the assets, we consider the gross book value of the debtors. Debtors worth ₹ 8,000 proved bad, so the remaining amount was fully realized. The realized amount is therefore ₹ 60,000 - ₹ 8,000 = ₹ 52,000. The provision of ₹ 3,000 has no bearing on the cash realization.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (C) है। विघटन के समय ₹ 60,000 के कुल देनदारों से वसूली की गणना होती है। ₹ 8,000 के देनदार डूब गए, अतः शेष देनदारों से प्राप्त राशि = ₹ 60,000 - ₹ 8,000 = ₹ 52,000 होगी।

questions.text: अश्मित, वीना तथा रोहन एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 31 मार्च, 2024 को वीना सेवा निवृत्त हो गयी। पुनर्मूल्यांकन, ख्याति, संचयों आदि से संबंधित सभी समायोजनों के पश्चात अश्मित, वीना तथा रोहन के पूँजी खातों में क्रमशः ₹ 2,00,000, ₹ 1,80,000 तथा ₹ 1,20,000 के जमा शेष थे। वीना को भुगतान अश्मित तथा रोहन द्वारा लाये गये रोकड़ के द्वारा इस प्रकार किया गया कि उनकी पूँजी उनके नये लाभ विभाजन अनुपात में हो जाये। अश्मित तथा रोहन की नयी पूँजी होगी :
questions.text_english: Ashmit, Veena and Rohan were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:1. Veena retired on 31st March, 2024. The capital accounts of Ashmit, Veena and Rohan showed a credit balance of ₹ 2,00,000, ₹ 1,80,000 and ₹ 1,20,000 respectively after making all adjustments relating to revaluation, goodwill, reserves etc. Veena was paid in cash brought in by Ashmit and Rohan in such a way that their capitals were in proportion to their new profit sharing ratio. The new capitals of Ashmit and Rohan will be :
questions.solution: The correct option is (A). With Veena retiring, the new profit sharing ratio for Ashmit and Rohan becomes 3:1. The total capital of the newly constituted firm is the sum of the adjusted capitals of all partners, since the continuing partners bring in cash equal to the retiring partner's payout. Total Capital = ₹ 2,00,000 + ₹ 1,80,000 + ₹ 1,20,000 = ₹ 5,00,000. Distributing this in the 3:1 ratio gives Ashmit: ₹ 5,00,000 × 3/4 = ₹ 3,75,000, and Rohan: ₹ 5,00,000 × 1/4 = ₹ 1,25,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। नई फर्म की कुल पूँजी तीनों साझेदारों की समायोजित पूँजी के योग के बराबर होगी (₹ 5,00,000)। इसे अश्मित और रोहन के नए अनुपात 3:1 में बाँटने पर अश्मित की पूँजी ₹ 3,75,000 और रोहन की ₹ 1,25,000 होगी।

questions.text: नीता, विदुर तथा मीता एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 3:4:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2024 को उन्होंने समीर को एक नया साझेदार बनाने का निर्णय किया। नीता, विदुर, मीता तथा समीर का नया लाभ विभाजन अनुपात अब 1:1:1:1 होगा। समीर के प्रवेश से पूर्व नीता, विदुर तथा मीता का स्थिति विवरण मशीनरी का ₹ 6,00,000 का शेष दर्शा रहा था। प्रवेश की तिथि को यह पाया गया कि मशीनरी का मूल्यांकन 20% अधिक दर्शाया गया है। समीर के प्रवेश के बाद नये स्थिति विवरण में दर्शाया जाने वाला मशीनरी का मूल्य होगा :
questions.text_english: Nita, Vidur and Mita were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:4:1. On 1st April 2024, they decided to admit Samir as a new partner. The new profit sharing ratio between Nita, Vidur, Mita and Samir will now be 1:1:1:1. The balance sheet of Nita, Vidur and Mita before Samir's admission showed machinery at ₹ 6,00,000. On the date of admission, it was found that the machinery is overvalued by 20%. The value of machinery shown in the new Balance Sheet after Samir's admission will be:
questions.solution: The correct option is (D). Let the true value of the machinery be 'x'. The book value is 20% more than the true value, which means x + 0.20x = ₹ 6,00,000. This simplifies to 1.20x = ₹ 6,00,000. Solving for x gives x = ₹ 6,00,000 / 1.20 = ₹ 5,00,000. The newly constituted firm will record the machinery at its true value in the new Balance Sheet.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (D) है। माना मशीनरी का सही मूल्य 'x' है, तो x + x का 20% = ₹ 6,00,000 होगा। 1.20x = ₹ 6,00,000. इसलिए x = ₹ 6,00,000 / 1.20 = ₹ 5,00,000. नई फर्म के स्थिति विवरण में मशीनरी इसके सही मूल्य पर दिखाई जाएगी।

questions.text: सारा तथा तारा एक फर्म के साझेदार थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2023 को उनकी पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 6,00,000 तथा ₹ 4,00,000 थी। 1 अक्टूबर, 2023 को तारा ने व्यक्तिगत उपयोग के लिए ₹ 1,00,000 का आहरण किया। साझेदारी संलेख के अनुसार पूँजी पर ब्याज 8% वार्षिक दर से देय था। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए तारा की पूँजी पर दिये गये ब्याज की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Sara and Tara were partners in a firm. Their capitals as on 1st April, 2023 were ₹ 6,00,000 and ₹ 4,00,000 respectively. On 1st October, 2023, Tara withdrew ₹ 1,00,000 for personal use. According to the partnership deed, interest on capital was allowed @ 8% p.a. The amount of interest allowed on Tara's capital for the year ended 31st March, 2024 was:
questions.solution: The correct option is (A). Tara's interest on capital is calculated in two phases. For the first six months (April to September), interest is calculated on ₹ 4,00,000 at 8% p.a., resulting in ₹ 16,000. For the next six months (October to March), interest is calculated on the reduced capital of ₹ 3,00,000 at 8% p.a., amounting to ₹ 12,000. Total interest is ₹ 16,000 + ₹ 12,000 = ₹ 28,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। प्रथम छः माह (अप्रैल से सितम्बर) के लिए ₹ 4,00,000 पर 8% की दर से ब्याज ₹ 16,000 होगा। अगले छः माह (अक्टूबर से मार्च) के लिए घटी हुई पूँजी ₹ 3,00,000 पर 8% की दर से ब्याज ₹ 12,000 होगा। कुल देय ब्याज ₹ 28,000 होगा।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : फर्म के व्यवसाय को चलाने वाला प्रत्येक साझेदार फर्म के अन्य साझेदारों के लिए प्रमुख साझेदार तथा अभिकर्ता होता है।
कारण (R) : सभी साझेदारों के मध्य आपस में एक पारस्परिक एजेंसी का संबंध विद्यमान है।
निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Each partner carrying on the business of the firm is the principal as well as the agent for all the other partners of the firm.
Reason (R) : There exists a relationship of mutual agency between all the partners.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: दोनों अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: दोनों अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.

questions.solution: The correct option is (A). Mutual agency is the core defining principle of a partnership. This means every partner acts as an agent (binding others by their acts) and a principal (being bound by the acts of others). Thus, the Reason accurately and fully explains the Assertion.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। साझेदारी का मूल सिद्धांत पारस्परिक एजेंसी है, जिसका अर्थ है कि प्रत्येक साझेदार एक अभिकर्ता और एक प्रमुख दोनों के रूप में कार्य करता है। अतः कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है।

sub_questions.text_english: Kartik, Inder and Lalit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:3:2. With effect from 1st April, 2024, they decided to share profits and losses in the ratio of 2:3:4. For this purpose, the goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 1,80,000. The necessary journal entry to show the effect of the above will be:

options.A: Lalit's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000 To Kartik's Capital A/c 40,000
options.B: Kartik's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000 To Lalit's Capital A/c 40,000
options.C: Lalit's Capital A/c Dr. 1,80,000 To Kartik's Capital A/c 1,80,000
options.D: Kartik's Capital A/c Dr. 1,80,000 To Lalit's Capital A/c 1,80,000

options_english.B: Kartik's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000 To Lalit's Capital A/c 40,000
options_english.C: Lalit's Capital A/c Dr. 1,80,000 To Kartik's Capital A/c 1,80,000
options_english.D: Kartik's Capital A/c Dr. 1,80,000 To Lalit's Capital A/c 1,80,000

sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (A). Comparing the old ratio (4:3:2) and new ratio (2:3:4), Kartik sacrifices 2/9 of his share (4/9 - 2/9) and Lalit gains 2/9 of the share (4/9 - 2/9). The gaining partner (Lalit) compensates the sacrificing partner (Kartik). The compensation is calculated on the firm's goodwill: ₹ 1,80,000 × 2/9 = ₹ 40,000. Therefore, Lalit's Capital A/c is debited and Kartik's Capital A/c is credited with ₹ 40,000.

questions.text_english: Moksh and Pran were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 1:2. Their capitals were ₹ 5,00,000 and ₹ 3,00,000 respectively. They admitted Tushar as a new partner on 1st April, 2024 for 1/4th share in future profits. Tushar brought ₹ 4,00,000 as his share of capital. The goodwill of the firm on Tushar's admission will be :
questions.solution: The correct option is (B). Hidden goodwill is determined by subtracting the actual combined capital of all partners from the capitalized value of the new firm. Based on Tushar's share, total capitalized value = ₹ 4,00,000 × (4/1) = ₹ 16,00,000. Actual combined capital = ₹ 5,00,000 + ₹ 3,00,000 + ₹ 4,00,000 = ₹ 12,00,000. Hidden goodwill = ₹ 16,00,000 - ₹ 12,00,000 = ₹ 4,00,000.

questions.text: पीयूष, आदी तथा सुधा एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 4:3:3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 1 अक्टूबर, 2024 को आदी की मृत्यु हो गयी। साझेदारी संलेख के अनुसार मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभ-हानि में आदी के भाग की गणना विक्रय के आधार पर की जायेगी। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष का विक्रय ₹ 6,00,000 था तथा 1 अप्रैल से 30 सितम्बर, 2024 तक यह ₹ 2,00,000 था। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए लाभ की गणना ₹ 1,50,000 की गयी। लेखा पुस्तकें प्रति वर्ष 31 मार्च को बंद की जाती हैं। फर्म के लाभ में आदी के भाग की गणना कीजिए तथा इसके लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टि भी कीजिए। अपना कार्य स्पष्टता से दर्शाइये।
questions.text_english: Piyush, Aadi and Sudha were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:3:3. Aadi died on 1st October, 2024. As per the partnership deed, Aadi's share of profit or loss till the date of death was to be calculated on the basis of sales. Sales for the year ended 31st March, 2024 amounted to ₹ 6,00,000 and that from 1st April to 30th September, 2024 amounted to ₹ 2,00,000. The profit for the year ending 31st March, 2024 was calculated as ₹ 1,50,000. The books of accounts are closed on 31st March every year. Calculate Aadi's share of profits in the firm and pass necessary journal entries for the same. Show your working clearly.

key_points: Calculation of Percentage of Profit to Sales for the previous year (25%).
Calculation of Estimated Profit for the 6-month period till death (₹ 50,000).
Calculation of Aadi's share of profit (₹ 15,000).
Journal Entry debiting P&L Suspense A/c and crediting Aadi's Capital A/c with ₹ 15,000.

questions.solution:
Working Notes:
First, we determine the profit margin based on the previous year's performance. The previous year's profit was ₹ 1,50,000 on sales of ₹ 6,00,000. 
Percentage of Profit to Sales = (₹ 1,50,000 / ₹ 6,00,000) × 100 = 25%.
Next, we calculate the firm's estimated profit from 1st April 2024 to 30th September 2024. The sales for this period were ₹ 2,00,000.
Estimated Profit = 25% of ₹ 2,00,000 = ₹ 50,000.
Finally, we calculate Aadi's share of this profit using his profit-sharing ratio (3/10).
Aadi's Share = ₹ 50,000 × 3/10 = ₹ 15,000.

Journal Entry (on 1st Oct 2024):
Profit and Loss Suspense A/c  Dr.  ₹ 15,000
    To Aadi's Capital A/c                   ₹ 15,000
(Being Aadi's share of profit till the date of his death credited to his capital account)

The firm of Amish, Nitish and Misha, who have been sharing profits in the ratio of 2:2:1, have existed for some years. Misha wanted that she should get equal share in the profits with Amish and Nitish and she further wished that the change in the profit sharing ratio should come into effect retrospectively for the last three years. Amish and Nitish had agreement for this.
The profits for the last three years were:
2021-22  ₹ 1,15,000
2022-23  ₹ 1,24,000
2023-24  ₹ 2,11,000
Show adjustment of profits by means of a single adjustment journal entry. Show your working clearly.

key_points: Total profits of three years calculated as ₹ 4,50,000
Old distribution of profits in 2:2:1 (Amish ₹ 1,80,000, Nitish ₹ 1,80,000, Misha ₹ 90,000)
New distribution of profits in 1:1:1 (Amish ₹ 1,50,000, Nitish ₹ 1,50,000, Misha ₹ 1,50,000)
Net adjustment: Amish Dr ₹ 30,000, Nitish Dr ₹ 30,000, Misha Cr ₹ 60,000
Single adjustment entry with correct accounts and amounts

sub_questions.solution:
Working Note:
The total profit of the last three years is ₹ 1,15,000 + ₹ 1,24,000 + ₹ 2,11,000 = ₹ 4,50,000. These profits were originally credited to the partners in the ratio 2:2:1, giving Amish ₹ 1,80,000, Nitish ₹ 1,80,000, and Misha ₹ 90,000. However, the profits should have been shared equally (1:1:1), giving each partner ₹ 1,50,000.
Comparing the two distributions: Amish received an excess of ₹ 30,000 (1,80,000 - 1,50,000) and Nitish received an excess of ₹ 30,000. Misha suffered a shortfall of ₹ 60,000 (1,50,000 - 90,000). To rectify this retrospectively, Amish and Nitish must be debited and Misha credited.

Journal Entry:
Amish's Capital A/c   Dr.  ₹ 30,000
Nitish's Capital A/c  Dr.  ₹ 30,000
    To Misha's Capital A/c            ₹ 60,000
(Being adjustment entry passed for retrospective effect of change in profit sharing ratio)

sub_questions.text_english: Delight Ltd. purchased assets worth ₹ 4,00,000 and took over liabilities of ₹ 70,000 of Marvel Ltd. for a purchase consideration of ₹ 3,60,000. Delight Ltd. paid the purchase consideration by issuing 11% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a premium of 20%. Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Delight Ltd.

key_points: Calculation of Goodwill: Net Assets = 4,00,000 - 70,000 = 3,30,000. Purchase consideration is 3,60,000. Goodwill = 30,000.
Entry for taking over business, including debit to Goodwill A/c.
Calculation of debentures to be issued: 3,60,000 / 120 = 3,000 debentures.
Entry for the issue of debentures to the vendor at a premium.

sub_questions.solution:
In the books of Delight Ltd., the first entry records the acquisition of assets and liabilities. The net assets acquired amount to ₹ 3,30,000 (Assets ₹ 4,00,000 - Liabilities ₹ 70,000). Since the purchase consideration of ₹ 3,60,000 exceeds the net assets acquired, the difference of ₹ 30,000 is recognized as Goodwill. The purchase consideration is discharged by issuing 11% debentures at a 20% premium (Issue price = ₹ 120). Therefore, the number of debentures issued is ₹ 3,60,000 / 120 = 3,000 debentures.

Journal Entries:
1. Assets A/c                   Dr.  ₹ 4,00,000

     To Liabilities A/c                     ₹ 70,000
     To Marvel Ltd.                         ₹ 3,60,000
(Being assets and liabilities taken over and goodwill recorded)

2. Marvel Ltd.                  Dr.  ₹ 3,60,000

     To Securities Premium A/c              ₹ 60,000
(Being 3,000, 11% debentures issued at a premium of 20% to discharge the purchase consideration)

questions.text: सीमा तथा अवि की फर्म की पूँजी ₹ 12,00,000 है तथा ब्याज की बाज़ार दर 10% है। प्रत्येक साझेदार का वेतन प्रति वर्ष ₹ 10,000 है। पिछले चार वर्षों के लाभ क्रमशः ₹ 3,00,000, ₹ 4,00,000, ₹ 5,00,000 तथा ₹ 4,00,000 थे। फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन पिछले चार वर्षों के औसत अधिलाभ के तीन वर्षों के क्रय के आधार पर किया जायेगा। फर्म की ख्याति की गणना कीजिए।
questions.text_english: The capital of the firm of Seema and Avi is ₹ 12,00,000 and the market rate of interest is 10%. Salary of each partner is ₹ 10,000 per annum. The profits for the last four years were ₹ 3,00,000, ₹ 4,00,000, ₹ 5,00,000 and ₹ 4,00,000 respectively. Goodwill of the firm is to be valued on the basis of three years purchase of last four years average super profits. Calculate the goodwill of the firm.

key_points: Calculate Normal Profit: ₹ 12,00,000 × 10% = ₹ 1,20,000
Deduct annual partners' salaries (₹ 20,000) to find Adjusted Average Profit: ₹ 3,80,000
Calculate Super Profit: ₹ 3,80,000 - ₹ 1,20,000 = ₹ 2,60,000
Calculate Goodwill: Super Profit (₹ 2,60,000) × 3 years = ₹ 7,80,000

questions.solution:
The goodwill valuation using the super profit method requires computing normal profit and adjusted average profit. First, normal profit is calculated on the capital employed (₹ 12,00,000) at the normal rate of return (10%), which gives ₹ 1,20,000. Next, the average profit of the past four years is computed: (₹ 3,00,000 + ₹ 4,00,000 + ₹ 5,00,000 + ₹ 4,00,000) / 4 = ₹ 16,00,000 / 4 = ₹ 4,00,000. From this average profit, we must deduct the partners' salaries to find the adjusted business profit. The total salary for two partners is ₹ 10,000 × 2 = ₹ 20,000. Thus, the adjusted average profit is ₹ 4,00,000 - ₹ 20,000 = ₹ 3,80,000.

The super profit is the difference between adjusted average profit and normal profit: ₹ 3,80,000 - ₹ 1,20,000 = ₹ 2,60,000. Finally, goodwill is calculated based on three years' purchase of super profits: ₹ 2,60,000 × 3 = ₹ 7,80,000. The firm's goodwill is ₹ 7,80,000.

questions.text_english:
Raja, Bharat and Vedika were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:2:1. Their Balance Sheet as on 31st March, 2024 was as follows:
[Balance Sheet Table in Image]
Vedika died on 31st July, 2024. According to the partnership deed, her legal representatives are entitled to the following:
(i) Balance in her capital account
(ii) Interest on capital @ 8% p.a.
(iii) Her share in the profit upto the date of death to be calculated on the basis of last year's profit. Vedika's share of profit was ₹ 3,000.
(iv) Her share of goodwill calculated on the basis of two years purchase of average profits of last three years. The average profit of last three years was ₹ 40,000. Vedika's drawings upto the date of death were ₹ 12,000.
Prepare Vedika's Capital Account to be rendered to her executors.

key_points: Opening balance (Credit): ₹ 90,000
Share of General Reserve (Credit): 1/5th of ₹ 50,000 = ₹ 10,000
Interest on capital (Credit): ₹ 90,000 × 8% × 4/12 = ₹ 2,400
Share of profit till death (Credit): ₹ 3,000
Share of goodwill (Credit): Total GW = 40,000 × 2 = 80,000. Share = 80,000 × 1/5 = 16,000
Drawings (Debit): ₹ 12,000
Final balance transferred to Vedika's Executor's A/c: ₹ 1,09,400

questions.solution:
To prepare Vedika's Capital Account to be rendered to her executors, we post the required credits and debits as of the date of her death on 31st July 2024 (4 months into the financial year).

Vedika's Capital Account will be credited with her opening balance as per the Balance Sheet, which is ₹ 90,000. She is entitled to her 1/5th share of the General Reserve from the Balance Sheet (₹ 50,000), which equals ₹ 10,000. Interest on her capital for 4 months is computed at 8% per annum on ₹ 90,000, contributing ₹ 2,400. Her predefined share in the profit till the date of death is given as ₹ 3,000. For goodwill, the firm's goodwill is valued at 2 years' purchase of the average profit of ₹ 40,000, amounting to ₹ 80,000. Vedika's 1/5th share is ₹ 16,000, which will be credited to her account (to be borne by continuing partners). 

On the debit side, Vedika's drawings during the period up to her death amount to ₹ 12,000. Summarizing these entries: total credits sum up to ₹ 1,21,400 (90,000 + 10,000 + 2,400 + 3,000 + 16,000) and the total debit is ₹ 12,000. The net balancing figure of ₹ 1,09,400 is transferred to Vedika's Executor's Account.

key_points: Capital Employed = Shareholders Funds + Non-Current Liabilities = 16,00,000 + 8,00,000 = 24,00,000.
Net Profit Before Tax = Net Profit After Tax + Tax = 3,00,000 + 1,00,000 = 4,00,000.
Interest on Debentures = 10% of 8,00,000 = 80,000.
EBIT = Net Profit Before Tax + Interest = 4,00,000 + 80,000 = 4,80,000.
Return on Investment = (EBIT / Capital Employed) × 100 = (4,80,000 / 24,00,000) × 100 = 20%.

sub_questions.solution:
Return on Investment (ROI) is calculated by dividing Profit Before Interest and Tax (EBIT) by Capital Employed, multiplied by 100. 

First, calculate Capital Employed. Using the liabilities approach, Capital Employed = Shareholders Funds + Non-Current Liabilities (10% Debentures) = ₹ 16,00,000 + ₹ 8,00,000 = ₹ 24,00,000.
Next, calculate EBIT. The Net Profit After Tax is ₹ 3,00,000, and Tax paid is ₹ 1,00,000, which means Net Profit Before Tax is ₹ 4,00,000. To find EBIT, we must add back the interest on long-term debt. Interest on the 10% Debentures of ₹ 8,00,000 is ₹ 80,000. So, EBIT = ₹ 4,00,000 + ₹ 80,000 = ₹ 4,80,000.

Now, substitute these into the ROI formula: (₹ 4,80,000 / ₹ 24,00,000) × 100 = 20%. Therefore, the Return on Investment is 20%.

sub_questions.text_english: Calculate Cash Flows from Investing Activities...

key_points: Machine sold: Book Value = 50,000 - 20,000 = 30,000. Sale Value = 30,000 + 10% profit = 33,000 (Inflow).
Machinery Account: Opening balance 3,00,000. Less cost of machine sold 50,000 = 2,50,000. Closing balance is 3,80,000. So, purchase of Machinery = 1,30,000 (Outflow).
Net Cash Used in Investing Activities = 33,000 (Inflow) - 1,30,000 (Outflow) = (97,000).

sub_questions.solution:
First, we determine the cash inflow from the sale of machinery. The book value of the sold machine is its cost (₹ 50,000) minus its accumulated depreciation (₹ 20,000), which is ₹ 30,000. It was sold at a 10% profit on book value, meaning the profit is ₹ 3,000. Thus, the total sale proceeds are ₹ 30,000 + ₹ 3,000 = ₹ 33,000.

Next, we determine the cash outflow for the purchase of machinery. We prepare a Machinery Account at cost. The opening balance is ₹ 3,00,000. We credit the account with the original cost of the machine sold, which is ₹ 50,000. The closing balance is given as ₹ 3,80,000. To balance the account, there must be a debit representing the purchase of new machinery. Purchase = Closing Balance (₹ 3,80,000) + Machine Sold (₹ 50,000) - Opening Balance (₹ 3,00,000) = ₹ 1,30,000 (Outflow).

The Net Cash Flow from Investing Activities is the sum of these flows. It equals ₹ 33,000 (Inflow from Sale) - ₹ 1,30,000 (Outflow for Purchase) = (₹ 97,000). Thus, net cash used in investing activities is ₹ 97,000.

sub_questions.text_english: Calculate Cash flows from Financing Activities...

key_points: Issue of Equity Share Capital = 12,00,000 - 8,00,000 = 4,00,000 (Inflow).
Increase in Securities Premium = 1,40,000 - 1,00,000 = 40,000 (Inflow). Total receipt from issue = 4,40,000.
Redemption of 11% Debentures = 4,00,000 - 3,00,000 = 1,00,000 (Outflow).
Interest paid on Debentures = 40,000 (Outflow).
Net Cash Flow from Financing Activities = 4,40,000 - 1,00,000 - 40,000 = 3,00,000 (Inflow).

sub_questions.solution:
To calculate the net cash flows from financing activities, we observe the changes in equity and long-term borrowing balances. 

Equity Share Capital increased from ₹ 8,00,000 to ₹ 12,00,000 during the year, indicating a new issue of shares that generated a cash inflow of ₹ 4,00,000. At the same time, the Securities Premium increased from ₹ 1,00,000 to ₹ 1,40,000, representing an additional inflow of ₹ 40,000 received as premium on these issued shares. The total cash inflow from the issue of shares is ₹ 4,40,000.

The balance of 11% Debentures decreased from ₹ 4,00,000 to ₹ 3,00,000, representing a redemption of debentures which is a cash outflow of ₹ 1,00,000. Furthermore, the interest paid on these debentures is specified as ₹ 40,000, which is also a cash outflow under financing activities.

Summing these items up: ₹ 4,40,000 (Inflow from Shares) - ₹ 1,00,000 (Outflow for Redemption) - ₹ 40,000 (Outflow for Interest) = ₹ 3,00,000. Therefore, the net cash inflow from financing activities is ₹ 3,00,000.

questions.text_english: What is meant by 'Data', 'Information' and 'Transaction'?

key_points: Data refers to raw, unprocessed facts, figures, and details.
Information is processed, organised, and structured data that provides meaningful context and aids in decision-making.
Transaction is an economic event or business activity that involves the exchange of values and impacts the financial position of the business.

questions.solution:
Data refers to the raw, unorganized, and unprocessed facts, figures, numbers, or observations that lack specific meaning in isolation. It serves as the basic input for any processing system. 

Information is data that has been processed, structured, and presented in a meaningful and useful context, enabling management and users to make informed decisions and draw conclusions.

A Transaction is a specific economic event or business activity entered into by an enterprise that involves a transfer or exchange of money, goods, or services, and which objectively alters the financial state of the business, necessitating a record in the books of accounts.

questions.text_english: List six features of an Accounting Software.

key_points: Speed and Accuracy in processing data.

Security measures such as passwords and data encryption.

questions.solution:
Six key features of an Accounting Software include:
1. Speed and Accuracy: It processes vast amounts of numerical data rapidly and practically eliminates human mathematical errors.
2. Automated Document Production: It can automatically generate essential accounting documents like invoices, receipts, and account statements.
3. Real-time Updating: Entering a transaction instantly updates all related ledgers, trial balances, and financial statements without manual posting.
4. Scalability: It can seamlessly accommodate a growing volume of business transactions without proportionally increasing the administrative burden.
5. Security and Access Control: It offers robust data protection through password controls, user permissions, and database encryption.
6. Flexible Reporting: It allows users to quickly generate diverse, customized, and comparative financial reports at any point in time.

sub_questions.text_english: Each and every data from Notepad file can be saved as an Excel data file. This provides a lead that Excel worksheet consists of four types of data in cell. Name and state these data types.

key_points: Text Data: Contains alphanumeric characters used for labels and descriptions.
Number Data: Numeric values used for mathematical calculations.
Date and Time Data: Values formatted specifically to represent dates and times, which can be manipulated chronologically.
Formula Data: Mathematical expressions or functions used to calculate results based on other cells.

sub_questions.solution:
An Excel worksheet generally accommodates four primary types of data within its cells:
1. Text (Labels): This includes alphabetic characters, symbols, or alphanumeric combinations that are generally used for headings, names, or descriptive data that is not subjected to mathematical calculations.
2. Numbers (Values): These are purely numeric entries (including decimals) that Excel recognizes as quantities, allowing users to perform arithmetic operations on them.
3. Dates and Times: Although stored internally as serial numbers, these are specific data types formatted to represent dates and times, allowing for chronological calculations and filtering.
4. Formulas/Functions: These are mathematical equations or built-in functions starting with an equal sign (=). They do not represent static data but dynamically calculate and display a result based on values stored in other cells.

sub_questions.text_english: What is meant by 'Data Validation'? What is facilitated by 'Error Alert Tab'?

key_points: Data Validation is a feature in Excel used to control and restrict what data a user can enter into a specific cell.
It ensures data accuracy and consistency.
The 'Error Alert Tab' allows the creator to set up custom warning messages.
It dictates how the system responds (Stop, Warning, or Information) when invalid data is entered, guiding the user to correct their input.

sub_questions.solution:
Data Validation is a crucial feature in spreadsheet software designed to restrict the type, format, or values of data that a user can enter into a specific cell. It acts as a preventative control to ensure data consistency and accuracy, such as restricting input to a specific date range, a whole number, or a dropdown list of pre-approved items.

The 'Error Alert' tab within the Data Validation dialog box facilitates customized feedback. It allows the designer to define the exact response the system should give when a user attempts to input invalid data. It provides three styles of alerts: 'Stop' (prevents the invalid entry entirely), 'Warning' (warns the user but allows them to proceed), and 'Information' (simply informs the user). It also allows the creation of a custom title and error message to instruct the user on the correct data format expected.

questions.text_english: If a user wishes to change a 'Text Option' as an element of chart, how can he/she do so? Explain.

questions.solution:
